# Course Overview:

*"You will ever remember that all the end of study is to make you a good man and a useful citizen." -John Adams*

Welcome to Consumer Insights. This course isn't just about marketing, it's about understanding people, choices, and change. Whether or not you plan to work in marketing, the principles you'll learn here shape every business decision and every career path.

Marketing is the bridge between ideas and impact. It's how businesses create value, how innovations reach the world, and how organizations connect with the people they serve. At its core, marketing is about solving problems, improving lives, and telling stories that matter.

Marketing isn't just about selling, it's about creating better products, better services, and helping people become who they aspire to be. This course will illustrate the importance of marketing and will help students develop knowledge and skills applicable to both professional aspirations and becoming wiser consumers. This course is in alignment with the learning goals of Cal Poly, the learning goals of the Orfalea College of Business, and the program goals of the Marketing concentration.

## Course Format

This project-based class will consist of interactive lectures and class discussions/activities/group projects. You are responsible for reading the required material *before* class in order to contribute to the class discussion. We will discuss real-world marketing situations and have in-class activities for the majority of the classes. Additionally, you will complete group assignments and a project to practice what you have learned.

**COREQUISITE: [This course has a required attached activity. You must be formally enrolled in both the course and its associated activity, regardless of whether you are following the quarter or semester catalog.]{.underline}**

Please check your official schedule in Student Center (not just Canvas) to confirm that both appear. [If you are not enrolled in both components by XXXX at 11:59 p.m., you will be dropped from the course.]{.mark}

PREREQUISITES: Prerequisite: Grade of C- or better in BUS 346

# Outcome Expectations

After completing this course students should be able to:

- Develop effective critical thinking and problem-solving skills and communicate skillfully in multiple forms of expression. (PLO 7, PLO 8 )
- Understand and apply marketing and psychology frameworks and tools to analyze information and influence consumer behaviors such as perceptions, affect, motivations, memory and the decision-making process etc. (PLO4, PLO5, PLO6, PLO7)
- Demonstrate an integrative knowledge of human and understand multiple dimensions of human experience, such as the ethical, culture, and religious dimensions (PLO4, PLO5, PLO6, PLO7, PLO9)
- Evaluate ethical topics and global issues in marketing. (PLO1, PLO6)

# Teaching Philosophy

My role is not just to teach you but to help you learn.  With this course, my goal is to provide you with ample opportunity to discover how businesses market to consumers and organizations.  Lectures, readings, presentations, mentors, guest speakers, activities, assignments, workshops, and exams are all meant to guide you toward active exploration and analysis of the principles of marketing. I am here to direct your learning, clarify concepts, and augment material.  Treat me as a resource---I encourage you to meet during office hours or communicate via e-mail with comments, questions, or concerns. Any suggestions on how to improve your learning experience are always welcome.

# Assignment Descriptions

## Class Participation/ Attendance/Class activities

Participation in lectures is expected in this class. Your participation grade will incorporate your attendance in lectures, how often you participate, and the quality of your participation.

In addition to the course textbook, learning for this course takes place through class discussions, class exercises, and class presentations by the instructor, guest speakers and students in the class. Therefore, I expect you to attend every class.

Class participation grades will be determined by class attendance and class conduct, but also by both quantity and quality of participation in class discussions (= 15 points). All students are encouraged to actively participate in class discussions by asking and answering questions and by offering ideas and suggestions.

## Group Assignments and Project:

Students will be placed into groups, with 4-5 students in each group, and complete a comprehensive *Consumer Insights* group project.

Refer to the assignment document on Canvas for more details. At the end of the semester, you will present a comprehensive report on your work.

## Teams

Each student will be assigned to a team during the FIRST WEEK OF CLASS. Although drops and adds may require some teams to be adjusted, the teams will remain together for the remainder of the semester. Working in a team can be both difficult and rewarding. It is oftentimes difficult to manage the various personalities and equitably distribute the work. Developing the necessary skills to work productively with a team, however, can be quite rewarding. If there are team problems, consult with me as soon as you realize your team is at an impasse. I can only help if I know you are having difficulty.

## Team Evaluations

Twice during the semester (mid-term and after final presentations), you will submit a peer eval to evaluate your teammates (a Qualtrics link will be posted to Canvas). Any individuals receiving negative feedback from teammates will have their score on the group project reduced. Be the teammate that you would most like to work with and you should be fine.

## Exams

All exams will be in-person closed-book, non-comprehensive Canvas exams using the lockdown browser. The exams will consist of multiple-choice questions from both the text and the lectures. Exams are held in class, and students need to be on time for all exams. Failure to take an exam on the scheduled day will result in a grade of zero. Please contact the DRC if you need extra time or accommodation.

## Research Essay

[The research essay invites you to explore the academic foundations of consumer behavior. By bridging theoretical research with practical application, you will develop a deeper understanding of how consumer insights influence real-world marketing strategies. This assignment aligns with our course goals of developing critical thinking skills and applying marketing frameworks to analyze human behavior.]{.mark}

Refer to the assignment document on Canvas for more details.

## Weekly Reflections

I am a firm believer that reflecting on our actions and our behaviors are the best way to make meaningful change and improvements. This class focuses on understanding the behaviors of others, but this weekly assignment will give you the chance to focus on and understand your own behaviors.

At the end of week 1, you will submit a short paragraph describing some consumption behavior that you want to track for yourself. The beauty of this assignment is that everything we do is consumption of something. Therefore, your reflections can be as simple as eating less, lifting heavier weights, or running a marathon. It can be focused on any domain of your life; you could commit to do less scrolling on your phone, or read a book each week. It can be anything, it just needs to be something that you can reasonably achieve. The goal here is to understand how you consume, so that you can hopefully improve yourself.

Each week you will be required to submit a single page reflection on your progress throughout that week. I recommend tracking your progress each day (this can be a few sentences) and then simply combining these daily reflections into one 'weekly reflection' document.

Using AI appropriately is a skill you will need to learn in today's business environment. Some of you may already feel proficient in using AI, so this assignment will be extra credit.

To earn extra credit, complete all 3 of the AI literacy modules (25 points combined). No partial credit will be given, this is an all or nothing extra credit assignment.

# Academic Integrity

Cal Poly will not tolerate academic cheating or plagiarism in any form. Learning to think and work independently is part of the educational process. Allowing another individual to complete assignments constitutes fraud and academic dishonesty. Finding material from the internet or other sources and presenting it as original is also dishonest. All forms of academic dishonesty, including cheating, plagiarism, and falsification of academic records are subject to disciplinary action. All work submitted for this class must be originally prepared for this class; work submitted for a previous course is unacceptable. Per university policy, any student found violating this policy will be dropped from the course or receive a grade of \"F.\"

## Artificial Intelligence Policy

Generative AI tools---software that creates new text, images, computer code, audio, video, and other content---are widely available. This policy governs all such tools, including those released during our term together.

You may use generative AI tools on assignments in this course when I explicitly permit you to do so. Otherwise, you should refrain from using such tools. The only approved AI-use assignment is the Group Project. Feel free to use AI in your study preparations, but AI is [not]{.underline} to be used in writing your weekly reflections, or in your Research Essay.

If you do use generative AI tools on assignments in this class, you must properly document and credit the tools themselves.

Please cite the tool you used, and document (in a separate document) any prompts that you used.

If you choose to use generative AI tools, please remember that they are typically trained on limited datasets that are often out-of-date. Additionally, generative AI datasets are trained on pre-existing material, including copyrighted material; therefore, relying on a generative AI tool may result in plagiarism or copyright violations.

Finally, keep in mind that the goal of generative AI tools is to produce content that seems to have been produced by a human, not to produce accurate or reliable content; therefore, relying on a generative AI tool may result in your submission of inaccurate content.

It is your responsibility---not the tool's---to assure the quality, integrity, and accuracy of work you submit in any college course.

Misuse or unauthorized usage of generative AI tools may constitute a violation of the CSU Standards for Student Conduct. Please communicate with me if there is any confusion regarding its usage for assignments, assessments, or any other coursework.

Please maintain integrity, for your learning, your personal character, and academic record.
